newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan mutual fund seeks 4bln rupees loan.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan mutual fund seeks 4bln rupees loan.

text.p: Pakistan's state-run National Investment Trust (NIT) open-ended mutual trust said on Wednesday it was seeking four billion rupees ($98.78 million) in loans to redeem claims and diversify investment.
NIT chairman Razi-ur-Rahman Khan told reporters that the mutual fund would arrange the loans from local and foreign financial institutions.
He said NIT needed the money to clear outstanding redemption claims to inject some demand in choice scrips, and to diversify its investment portfolio to interest-free fixed-income securities.

NIT, with investments of 35 billion rupees in the local capital market, came under severe pressure recently when it was hit by redemptions worth 12.5 billion rupees after a massive erosion of market capitalisation, Khan said.
He said NIT had re-purchased units worth 5.5 billion rupees by May 31 and hoped to pay off all individual claims by June 30.
"Not only will NIT pay off its unit holders, but the pressure on the stock market due to fear of selling by NIT will also subside, which will help to bring stability in the market," Khan said.
